setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Victim Or The Crime** (2 reviews): Reviewer says Victim actually opened the second set, and Gloria was the encore; Reviewer recalls Jerry stopping mid-song and leaving the stage, with Bob turning to his amps [11][12]
- **Gloria** (2 reviews): Reviewer bet four friends driving from Madison, WI that Gloria would be played at the Palace, and won; Jerry laughed at Bob, who was screaming his head off during the song [10][13]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Jerry's lead at the end of the song still gives the reviewer chills [13]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Named along with West LA Fadeaway and Masterpiece as first-set highlights [15]
- **Wave To The Wind** (1 review): Reviewer says it features a nice, meaty jam [9]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review): Reviewer felt aliens were arriving on the Deadship by the time the band reached it [15]
- **Drumz** (1 review): During the drums segment, the reviewer kept thinking of Jamaica [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **Gloria**: back after 491 archived shows (2334 days) [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1992-03-23.141787.sbd.miller.flac2496** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 162 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1992-03-23.155837.FOBAKGDAT.GatelyBrotmanAnonNoel.t-flac1648**: source not stated; 19 songs; 167 min [3]. Said about its sound: Microphones sound muffled during Loose Lucy [3]
- **gd92-03-23.sbd.zei.541.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 147 min; rated 4.11/5 by 18 [6]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds great; the reviewer had never seen a board of this show before; The soundboard recording does not do the show justice; reviewer would prefer a good audience tape [7][18]
- **gd1992-03-23.141808.sbd.cm.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 19 songs; 162 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer and friends drove from Madison, Wisconsin, listening to the 11/1/85 show along the way [10]
- Reviewer sensed tension between Jerry and Bob that night; it was their first show [12]
- Fans saw the band's trucks in a blistering snowstorm en route from Hamilton, matching the Cold Rain and Snow opener [15]
- Another group of friends from Knoxville was staying at the Kingsley Inn nearby; the first night's post-show was placid [16]
- Bruce played accordion, which the reviewer disliked; piano would suit Masterpiece and Cold Rain better [17]
- Reviewer, who attended eight shows including Nassau and Philly, rated this among the best of them [9]
- A killer first set was followed by a weak pre-drums stretch; post-space recovered but not to first-set level [10]
- Though the second set looks average on paper, its musicianship is among the best of 1992 [11]
- Reviewer ranks Jack Straw, Masterpiece and Morning Dew among the best they've heard, and this the best of ten shows seen [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1992-03-23.141787.sbd.miller.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [1]
- **gd1992-03-23.155837.FOBAKGDAT.GatelyBrotmanAnonNoel.t-flac1648**: taped by Recording by B. Gately; transferred by DAT provided by Dave Brotman Transfer by Anonymous Edited & Mastered (Adobe Audition) by Joe Noel January 23, 2022; source: Recording: (FOB) AKG 460 > Oade P/S > Panasonic SV255 > DAT [3]. Also: Each tape was adjusted electronically and mechanically in an SV3800 for proper play; none have emphasis [3]
- **gd92-03-23.sbd.zei.541.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> D->CDR-> EAC> SHN [6]. Also: Disc one carries the start of set two plus the encore, apparently to fit everything on two discs; Reviewer wants a Miller remaster; the start of Crazy Fingers is stuck on the end of Wave To The Wind track [7][17]
- **gd1992-03-23.141808.sbd.cm.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [2]
